filename: Estimating historical air-sea CO2 fluxes_ Incorporating physical knowledge within a data-only approach _ ESS Open Archive.pdf
title: Estimating historical air-sea CO2 fluxes: Incorporating physical knowledge within a data-only approach
venue: ESS Open Archive (submitted to Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems)
code_availability: Python scripts are made available at https://github.com/valbennington/JAMES_pub_2022
testbed_rationale: The study produces an observation-based reconstructed surface pCO2 and air-sea CO2 flux product (gap-filling), rather than training an online parameterization or process emulator suitable for climate models.
pain_points: Sparsity of in situ pCO2 observations across the Southern Ocean and during winter months.
Lack of continuous satellite chlorophyll-a observations prior to 1998 requiring climatological substitution.
Uncertainties in wind speed products and gas transfer velocity (piston velocity) dominating flux calculation errors.
Non-linear competing effects of temperature (thermodynamic solubility vs. biology/stratification) confounding ML reconstruction.
extraction_notes: The paper uses XGBoost to learn the non-thermal component of pCO2 (pCO2 - pCO2_T), removing direct temperature dependence via Takahashi et al. formulation. Self-organizing maps (SOMPY) were also tested for clustering but found not to improve skill.
